chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Shihab, from Ibn Bukayr and Zurara, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
Regarding a man who was compelled by necessity to eat a carcass or hunted prey, while he is in the state of Ihram, he said: He should eat the hunted prey and pay its ransom.

key_terms.مَيْتَةٍ: Carcass or dead animal not slaughtered according to ritual law
key_terms.مُحْرِمٌ: One in the state of Ihram (ritual consecration for Hajj or Umrah)
key_terms.يَفْدِي: Pays ransom (compensation in kind or value for the hunted animal)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a pilgrim in Ihram who eats hunted game out of necessity?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the fiqh of necessity (darurah) for a pilgrim in Ihram, distinguishing between the permissibility of consuming hunted game and the obligation of expiation (fadyah). This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential principle that while the prohibition of meat remains, the specific penalty applies to the act of hunting or consuming game, whereas consuming a carcass does not incur the same ransom. The narration highlights the balance between preserving life and maintaining the sanctity of the pilgrimage rites.
